agentCan: Implement the authorize/token/refresh/revoke flow including refresh-token rotation persistence
Prepare app details and the directory-listing application email

approval.cost: None stated anywhere in the docs read
approval.trigger: OAuth apps are Private by default, 'meaning only members of your own Close organization can authorize them': the pre-approval cap is your own org only (no numeric cap stated). To go external: Settings > Developer > OAuth Apps, select the app, click 'Make Public' and submit for review. 'We'll review your app and reply by email. Once approved, your app will be marked as Public and any Close user will be able to authorize it.' A separate optional listing in the Close Integrations Directory is applied for by emailing support@close.com (integration name/description, product link, what it does with Close, your OAuth App's Client ID); requirements: the integration 'must be publicly available (not internal-only)', 'must use OAuth 2.0 for authentication (not API keys)', and 'should provide clear value to Close users'.
approval.wait: None stated (no duration, SLA, or published review criteria for the Make Public review or the directory listing)

blockers.detail: 'All OAuth applications are granted the all.full_access offline_access scopes, providing the same level of access as API keys.' There are no granular or read-only scopes and no way to request less. The Help Center is blunt: 'Once allowed, the third party app will get full read/write access to your Close organization', and to 'Can I change the scope (permissions) of the access?': 'No.'
blockers.howToClear: No clearance exists; be transparent with customers about full access, and note Close invites scope feedback ('If you have a use case for different scopes, we'd like to hear about it').
blockers.title: Total scope ceiling: full access or nothing

blockers.detail: On refresh, 'the authorization server issues a new Refresh Token and the client must discard the old Refresh Token and replace it with the new one. The authorization server revokes the old Refresh Token after issuing a new one.' Failing to persist the new refresh token breaks the connection.
blockers.howToClear: Persist the replacement refresh token atomically on every refresh.
blockers.title: Refresh-token rotation

blockers.detail: Redirect URLs must be https/TLS: 'plain http:// URLs are not accepted'. No localhost exception is documented, which complicates local development callbacks.
blockers.howToClear: Use an HTTPS tunnel or deployed callback for development; there is no documented http path.
blockers.title: HTTPS-only redirect, no localhost exception documented

alternatives: Private OAuth App (the default; only members of your own Close organization can authorize it; internal tools only)
API keys (tied to a specific user and organization; positioned for 'scripts, internal tools, import jobs, and automations', not multi-customer products)
flavor.recommended: A Public OAuth App using the standard OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow
flavor.why: The object is an OAuth App created under Settings > Developer > OAuth Apps, yielding a client_id and client_secret. Close's docs state OAuth 2.0 is 'strongly recommended for user-facing integrations that multiple users will authenticate to', and for multi-customer products 'so each customer can authorize access to their own org'. Access permissions inherit from the specific user/membership associated with the token; the token response includes organization_id and user_id.

humanMust: Create the OAuth App and copy the Client ID and Client Secret at creation
Click 'Make Public' and submit for review before external customers can connect

(Recommended) Set up a dev/test organization first: existing users can create a free secondary organization; non-users can email support@close.com requesting a free Dev organization with a description of the app, workflow, and expected release timeline
name: Close
nuances: Access tokens live 1 hour (expires_in 3600); refresh tokens are present in the token response because all apps get the offline_access scope.
Terms of Service URL and Privacy Policy URL are documented as 'Optional for internal-only apps', implying they are expected for public apps.

User-side revocation: any user can cut you off at Settings > Accounts & Apps > Authorized Apps > Revoke Access; revocation 'will immediately cut off access to Close data to that integration', and the only restore path is re-authorization from your app.
'Your OAuth app continues to work regardless of whether your Close account's subscription is active, expired, or canceled.'
If a connecting customer uses Google Workspace, a policy_enforced error means their Workspace admin is blocking third-party app access and must allowlist it in the Google Admin console.
Close also offers an MCP server for AI agent integrations; auth is via the same API key / OAuth methods.
prerequisites: A Close organization (a free dev/test organization is recommended)
App Name and Description for the consent screen
Terms of Service URL and Privacy Policy URL (optional for internal-only apps; expected for public)

steps.detail: Existing Close users can create a free secondary organization; non-users can email support@close.com requesting a free Dev organization with a description of your OAuth app, the overall workflow, and your expected release timeline.
steps.time: Email round trip; no duration stated
steps.title: (Recommended) Set up a dev/test organization

steps.detail: Fill in app details: App Name (shown on the consent screen), App Description (1-2 sentences), Redirect URL (must be https/TLS; plain http:// is not accepted), Terms of Service URL and Privacy Policy URL.
steps.title: Create the OAuth App

steps.detail: Click Create and copy the Client ID and Client Secret.
steps.title: Copy the credentials

steps.detail: Send the user to app.close.com/oauth2/authorize/?client_id={client_id}&response_type=code (with your redirect URI). The user selects an organization on the consent screen and grants or declines; on approval Close redirects to your redirect_uri with the code in the code query parameter; on decline, with ?error=access_denied.
steps.title: Send the user to authorize

steps.detail: POST api.close.com/oauth2/token/ form-encoded with client_id, client_secret, grant_type=authorization_code, code. Access tokens live 1 hour (expires_in 3600). Call the API with Authorization: Bearer; revoke via POST api.close.com/oauth2/revoke/ when a user disables the integration.
steps.title: Exchange the code; call the API

steps.detail: Apps are Private by default (your org only). Settings > Developer > OAuth Apps > select the app > 'Make Public' and submit for review; Close reviews and replies by email. Once approved, any Close user can authorize it. Optionally, apply for the Integrations Directory listing by emailing support@close.com.
steps.title: Make the app Public (review)

tagline: Private by default: your OAuth app works only inside your own Close organization until a human 'Make Public' review (reply by email, no timeline stated) opens it to everyone. And every app gets full read/write access, because Close has exactly one scope level.

time.active: ~15 min of app setup + ~1 hr of flow code
time.total: Unknown: the Make Public review has no stated duration
